newsitem.title: USA: Ford files for Hertz initial public offering.
newsitem.headline: Ford files for Hertz initial public offering.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Friday its planned to sell less than 20 percent of its Hertz Corp. car rental unit in an initial public offering.

Ford said the offering, which had been long expected, will involve newly issued shares of Hertz common stock. A registration statement for the offering was filed Friday with the Securities and Exchange Commission in Washington.
The transaction will mark the end of Ford's three-year ownership of all of Hertz. Ford first invested in the Park Ridge, N.J.-based car rental giant in 1987 and acquired full control in 1994.

Ford spokesman Christian Vinyard said pricing of the Hertz shares was at least "several weeks" away. Last year, Ford filed for an initial offering in its Associates First Capital Corp. unit in February, and the shares were not priced until early May.

Vinyard said Ford was keeping more than 80 percent of Hertz so it can continue to consolidate Hertz' earnings on its books for tax purposes. Asked if Ford may sell more of its stake at a later date, he said that was "very premature to even think about right now."

"Investor interest in the rental car industry has increased dramatically," Ford Vice Chairman Ed Hagenlocker said in a statement. "We believe that it is now in the best interest of our shareholders to consider an initial public offering of Hertz."
